clue.text: Object in special case on stand

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing on another sits after it, so the special case follows the stand

parts.note: to stand something is to tolerate or take it
a case that breaks the rule

explanation.surface: An exhibit in a specially made display case sits on a stand.
explanation.definitionFit: To object is to raise a protest, and the idiom for raising a protest is to take exception.

clue.text: Cite 24 lies told originally about minor details

indicators.note: about is read as around or scattered, so the collected letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the answer to 24 down
taken as written

indicators.note: the original part of a word is its beginning, so only the opening letter of told is kept

parts.note: the first letter of told

explanation.surface: Someone quotes lies about trivial points, as in a pedantic argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Technicalities are small points of procedure or fine print, the trivial particulars that pedants fuss over.

clue.text: In retirement, look for ganja essentially to go inside joints

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word for look for is read backwards
the kept letter is placed within the reversed word

parts.note: to look for is to seek

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only the central letter of ganja is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of ganja

explanation.surface: A retired person hunts for cannabis to roll into joints.
explanation.walkthrough: Joints suggests cannabis cigarettes alongside ganja, but here it means the body's hinges. Ganja is cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Knees are hinged articulations in the legs, typical examples of the body's joints.

clue.text: Go steady with nurse — to begin with it's not demanding?

indicators.note: this places the abbreviation for nurse at the very start of the build

parts.note: EN is an Enrolled Nurse
a go is an attempt, a try
steady and even, as in a level voice

explanation.surface: Advice on dating a nurse: it starts off undemanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go steady' reads as the phrase for dating, but the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry-level job or course is a basic, introductory one requiring little experience, so it asks little of you.

clue.text: Completes horror film — animated short that's repugnant

indicators.note: animated means set in lively motion, so the letters of short are moved about

parts.note: Carrie is the 1976 horror film from Stephen King's novel
the letters of short, rearranged
an exclamation of disgust at something repugnant

explanation.surface: A film review: an animated short is as repugnant as a horror film.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry something through is to see it to the end, so the phrase is a synonym for finishes or completes.

clue.text: Tingling sensation when Nick returns with things found under Christmas tree?

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word for nick is read from right to left

parts.note: to nick is to make a small cut, a snip
with means along with, and
a cut fir tree sheds its needles onto the floor beneath

explanation.surface: Saint Nick comes back with the presents found under the Christmas tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick looks like Santa, and things under the tree look like presents; the question mark flags that it is the fallen needles instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The prickling feeling in a limb as circulation returns after it has gone numb is commonly called this.

clue.text: Short distance from a member of church

parts.note: to be in a club or party is to be a member of it
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A churchgoer lives only a short distance away.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a tiny unit of length, about two and a half centimetres, so it stands for a small span.

clue.text: Starmer to Reeves for one hour being broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, as seed is sown, so the letters are spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Keir Starmer gives Rachel Reeves an hour on air.
explanation.walkthrough: Keir Starmer, Prime Minister, lives at 10 Downing Street; Rachel Reeves, Chancellor of the Exchequer, lives next door at No 11.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prime Minister and Chancellor occupy adjoining houses on Downing Street, so each is the other's next-door resident.

clue.text: Regularly daub it with Flora Light spread — tasty!

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of daub is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of daub

indicators.note: spread as a verb means scattered about, so the brand name's letters are dispersed and reordered

parts.note: taken as written
Flora Light is a brand of low-fat margarine

explanation.surface: Smear it with Flora Light margarine and it tastes good.
explanation.walkthrough: Tasty seems to praise the food, but in British slang a tasty person is attractive, which is the sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for an attractive person; tasty is used in the same informal admiring way about someone good-looking.

clue.text: Caught station interrupting show again — things go downhill fast here

parts.note: C is caught in cricket scoring

indicators.note: to interrupt something is to break into its middle, so the abbreviation sits inside the other word

parts.note: to repeat a programme is to rerun it
STA is an abbreviation for station

explanation.surface: A TV channel is caught breaking into a repeat with a station announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cresta Run is a famous natural-ice toboggan course at St Moritz in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: Toboggan riders hurtle head-first down this Swiss ice track at very high speed, so it is a place for fast descents.

clue.text: Go up first for chicken wing?

indicators.note: the first letter for the following word is the only one used

parts.note: the opening letter of chicken
a bird's wing is one of its limbs

explanation.surface: Asking whether to tackle the chicken wing first.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb is to ascend, moving upwards on a slope, ladder or mountain.

clue.text: Unpleasant in-laws stay occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of the phrase is kept

parts.note: the even-placed letters of these words

explanation.surface: It is unpleasant when the in-laws come to stay, even occasionally.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something disagreeable or offensive, so they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Country India controlled

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to run a business is to control it

explanation.surface: A historical note that India once governed some land.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in western Asia, formerly known as Persia.

clue.text: Conversation in Siamese maybe translated into French

indicators.note: the word for the animal is given in the French language instead of English

parts.note: a Siamese is a breed of cat

explanation.surface: Someone's Siamese twin or cat is being rendered into French.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat is an informal talk between people, a light conversation.

clue.text: Drives twelve 6s on the spin — exhausted another crosses the line

parts.note: drives as a noun are attempts or goes

indicators.note: a spin turns something round, so the word for the length is read backwards

parts.note: 6 down is a short unit of length; twelve of them make a foot

indicators.note: exhausted means emptied, so the inside of the next word is removed leaving its two ends

parts.note: the first and last letters of another

explanation.surface: A cricket or golf scene: twelve sixes in a row, and a tired opponent crosses the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 refers to the answer at 6 down, a short distance; twelve of those make a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross the line is to overstep acceptable limits, which is what overdoing something to excess means.

clue.text: Heard seals and young birds

indicators.note: heard means listened to, so the word for seals counts by its pronunciation rather than its spelling

parts.note: signet rings carry seals used to stamp wax

explanation.surface: Someone heard seals barking alongside young birds.
explanation.walkthrough: Seals suggests the marine animals, but here they are the stamps on signet rings.
explanation.definitionFit: Cygnets are baby swans, the offspring of these large waterbirds.

clue.text: Band with famous singer making independent label agree, initially, to provide access to smack?

indicators.note: making one thing into another here means swapping the letter for independent out for a new pair

parts.note: a band of people is a gang
P!nk is a well-known American pop singer
I is the abbreviation for independent

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letters of label and agree are kept

parts.note: the first letters of label and agree

explanation.surface: A band joining a star singer and getting an indie label to sign on.
explanation.walkthrough: Smack suggests heroin, but a smack is also a small sailing boat; the gangplank lets you board it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangplank is the movable board bridging quay and vessel, so it lets people get onto a boat.

clue.text: Decline delivery

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fall or decrease, as in a sharp fall in sales
second meaning: the act of leaving a parcel or person somewhere

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read like refusing a parcel, but each is a separate meaning of the hyphenated word.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names both a sudden fall in level or numbers and the act of dropping goods or passengers at a place.

clue.text: Let nine off to be merciful

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A judge lets nine defendants walk free out of mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenient means tolerant and mild in punishment, which is the merciful attitude described.

clue.text: See 4
Hole where bogeys could be upsetting to Ernie Els — but not the Europeans

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over, so the remaining letters are thrown into a new order
but not means excluding, so certain letters are taken out of the phrase

parts.note: taken as written; Ernie Els is a South African golfer
E is the abbreviation for European, and each E in the phrase is removed

explanation.surface: Golf: a hole where Ernie Els might card bogeys, while the Europeans are absent.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernie Els and hole steer you to golf scores, but bogeys here are lumps of nasal mucus.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostril is an opening in the nose, which is where snot, called bogeys in British slang, collects.

clue.text: See 5
Record that a performer covers

indicators.note: to cover something is to hold it inside, so the letters sit within the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the end of that, all of a, and the start of performer

explanation.surface: A song that a performer does as a cover version is recorded.
explanation.walkthrough: Covers looks like the music sense of a cover version, but it signals the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To tape something is to record it on magnetic tape, and a tape is also a recording.

clue.text: Put extremely expensive roof back on the house

indicators.note: put back means returned to where it came from, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
back completes the phrase put back, signalling the string is read backwards
extremely refers to the extremes, the ends, so only the first and last letters of each word are kept

parts.note: the outer letters of expensive
the outer letters of roof

explanation.surface: Putting a very expensive roof back on a house.
explanation.walkthrough: On the house reads as part of the building scene, but it is the idiom for something given without charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the house is given by the establishment at no cost, so it costs nothing.

clue.text: Old outspoken sea dog's chance

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: outspoken means said out loud, so the word for sea counts by its sound as a single letter

parts.note: sea is pronounced like the letter C
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: An old, blunt-talking sailor gets his opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: Sea dog reads as an old sailor, but sea and dog are separate pieces. Chance is the verb meaning happen.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to chance means to happen by accident, and to occur is to happen.

clue.text: 6 cycling with a mate

indicators.note: cycling means going round in a loop, so the last letters of the word are rotated to the front

parts.note: the answer to 6 down
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone goes cycling with a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: China is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang, china plate stands for mate, so china means a friend or pal.

clue.text: I light up shop

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
an LED is a light-emitting diode

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper illuminates the store.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a store selling prepared foods, cheeses and cold meats.

clue.text: Melania tripped, ultimately stopping First Lady's escape

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so these letters go inside the other word

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letters of the two words are kept

parts.note: the final letters of Melania and tripped

explanation.surface: Melania Trump stumbles, ending the First Lady's getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: First Lady suggests Melania Trump, but it is the Bible's first woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to avoid or elude, which is what making an escape involves.

clue.text: Inspiring new design to fit plug in

indicators.note: a new design is a fresh arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An inspired new design lets you fit a plug in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uplifting raises the spirits and gives hope, which is what inspiring describes.

clue.text: They sought excitement in adult books after getting a bishop's 7 sins back to front

indicators.note: after places the adult and books abbreviations behind the earlier pieces
the final letter of the word for sins moves from the back round to the front

parts.note: 7 down's answer; on a chessboard the bishop starts next to this piece
to sin is to err
A is the abbreviation for adult
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Someone seeks thrills in adult books after a bishop confesses his neighbour's sins.
explanation.walkthrough: A bishop's neighbour on the chessboard's back row is the knight, here pluralised.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval wandering knights roamed in search of adventure and chivalrous deeds, the excitement the definition refers to.
